venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative:
**CCATL — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (MOD: JK, entered by Mya)

Saturday is here & it came with good vibes. Decent start to the beginning of shift. Let's make sure to groom tables as guests enjoy themselves.

Closers & barback came in at 8pm. DJ started up soon after — guests enjoyed the DJ set a lot. We had an influx of guests come in around 9pm when the music was getting started.

Remain curious with guests — these connections will keep us going. You might be busy on the first interaction, so make sure to touch by them during downtime.

Very consistent Saturday night! We leaned on BOH a lot. Barback had to leave around 10:30; kitchen closed at that time.

Smooth night overall! Coolers are off to defrost. BIG SHOUTOUT TO KEYSHAWN FOR HOLDING US DOWN TONIGHT!!

**Kitchen:** Great night & great family meal. Thank you for all your support — please communicate with FOH how we can also be a support.

**86'd/Low:** 86 High Noon, cider, wings, Coke.

**Favorite moment:** Getting a visit from Ash!

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.weather: Hot and humid, rained at some point
venues.narrative:
**CCNSH — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (MOD & Chef: KK/KE & JMS, entered by JO)

A little bit of a funky Saturday night. We were around $800 in sales at 7pm. We did the bulk of our sales from 9:30-11pm, had a steep drop-off for a little bit, then another decent pop around midnight-1am. Guests celebrating birthdays, a bachelorette party, and our regular weekend crowd just looking for a good time. DJ was amazing tonight — read the room, and the vibes were a lot of fun. Overall a fun night!

**Comps:** $63.05 / 0.6% (lower comps tonight to maximize sales).

**Kitchen:** Decent food sales — we want to see more and I believe we will achieve it. John-Michael over here killing it, we appreciate you chef!

**Favorite moment:** We had so much fun with our VIPs tonight. Minakshi Singh and Vikram Vij came in to celebrate their recent Michelin star! Having industry folks of that stature join us is always worth boasting about. You could tell they were dialed in observing service. Smiles all around — and solid compliments for the Champagne Lassi.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative:
**DVR — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (AM MOD: Maggie H & Josh; PM MOD: Carey & Lucas, entered by Carey — report typed 'Sunday' but covers Saturday 7/18 by post time)

**Sales split:** DC/AM $1,750.80 | D&C (PM) $14,279.47 | Garden/6A closed for event. Non-event net $16,030 vs target $17,710. **Events:** net event sales $15,872 (event food $11,123) — total net including events $31,902.27. Comps $444.38 / 2.77%. 188 guests (Tock, non-event); check avg on non-event sales ~$85.

**Event Notes:** We held a wedding reception/family-style dinner for Alex & Miles with 76 guests from 5pm-11pm in all spaces. The night kicked off in the Garden for happy hour with the group ready for the festivities. Lucas W & Rachael knocked out a plethora of passed apps and a massive family-style dinner — the group couldn't have been more pleased. Massive shoutout to the chefs and the entire event staff, going back and forth between spaces all night. The B&G and wedding planner thanked us at the end of the evening. Another successful wedding in the books! — Thank you Kelly

**D&C Notes:** Not as busy in the lobby as last night, but fully staffed across the board which created a uniquely calm flow for the evening. Thanks to the entire staff for knocking out their roles!

**DC/AM Notes:** Great day with Care Leite! We got rocked in the first couple hours of the morning that smoothed out into a cocktail pop. Finished the cold brew today. Thank you Felix!

**Kitchen:** Pretty steady night for the boys. Rachel and Lucas crushed the event. — Thanks Nate

**Favorite moment:** With the lobby fully staffed, I was allowed the freedom to speak with many tables, make subtle suggestions for service improvement, and be in multiple places for the team. A really nice feeling.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative:
**EV — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (MOD & Chef: Kyler and Steves, entered by stef)

**Sales:** Beverage $7,064 | Food $839 | Retail $66. Total net $7,969 vs target $7,191 (+10.8%). 239 guests. Comps $576.83 / 7.2% — lots of DNL and industry gifts tonight.

**Service Notes:** A busy Saturday that kept the room rolling. We had weird emptier lulls between turns at the 2-hour marks where half the room would be empty, then full with a waitlist. Led to some stacked tickets at the service well and maneuvering between new and old tables, but we made it work and made a lot of folks' nights.

**Top sellers:** Rosalie, Paper Wasp, Native Lion.

**Door Notes:** Humid rainy weather with slight thunderstorms. A mellower Saturday that had its bumping moments! At open, a 6-top walk-in from Rochester in town for the Noah Kahan concert (many concert-goers tonight, also for Ariana Grande). Full by 6:45pm with a large 8pm turn, flipping almost all of the room very quickly. Medium waitlist that never grew long. Around 9pm we squeezed in a 10-top for one round. 10pm marked the turn for smaller friend groups; 11:45pm transitioned back to 2-top nightcaps with a small 45-minute wait. Quieted down early at 12:30am, but got one last 7-top at 1:30am.

Industry guests: Eduardo from Gabriel Kreuther and Kiro from Tins with friends. Sean Abrams from GQ stopped in, plus members James Lupton and Elinor Humphreys (7-top birthday). Notable mentions: Curtis Allumbaugh visiting from PA who loved it so much he came back and teared up at the bar, Chelsie (local regular, CEO at Gigantic Studios), and two folks from Hawaii fresh from WWE matches.

**No-shows:** Philip Jackson for 2 at 8pm (not charged).

**Glassware breakage:** 3 chipped DOFs, 375 cheater, coupe.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative:
**LA — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (MOD & Chef: Gigi + Joe + Josh + Saleh; entered by Joe)

**Sales:** Net sales $12,233 vs target $11,890 (+2.9%). Food sales $2,146. Standing Room $2,807; Marquee $9,426. Comps $511 (Vic, Yiban, Bird, 40th birthday party, Ryan, Chef from Meteora, Kaneda, birthdays, anniversaries, investors, DNL, service recovery). Guests 316; check average $93.38. Weather: a humid day in LA.

**Notes:** A very busy Saturday night — opened with 116 covers plus lots of large-party reservations and walk-ins. Slow first hour, but by 7pm the entire room was filled and standing room built from there; big push at 8pm, then both rooms stayed full until 12:30am. Down a host, but Ruffy and Gigi held down the floor and host stand. Lots of familiar faces in for drinks; service flow felt great and never overwhelming. Kitchen: busy night. No incidents; no-shows charged.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.weather: Cooler, lightning storms and light rain, humid
venues.narrative:
**DC — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (MOD: Marcus)

**Sales split:** Marquee $9,033.93 gross | Garden $755.71. Total net including events $8,886.62 vs target $8,405 (+5.7%). 228 guests — 81 reservations, 147 walk-ins. Comps $60.30 (Community $37.30, DNL $23).

**Garden Notes:** We pushed the Garden opening back to 8pm due to the heat and poor air quality, and it ended up being the right call. Just as Marquee began filling up, we were able to direct guests to the Garden — cooler temps, light rain, and a breeze made the space much more comfortable. Around four groups joined between 8:00-8:15pm and it served well as overflow all evening. A couple of beers were accidentally rung to Marquee instead of the Garden — caught early, corrected, no waste. Fairly quiet by 10:30pm with a small overflow wave later; last call shortly after 11pm.

**D&C Notes:** Nice start with the dining room and bartop filling up around 6:30pm. Marquee hit a brief lull around 8:30pm before building back to a full room by 10:30pm. Very natural last call at 1:30am. The host team did a great job using the Garden as overflow and getting creative with seating. Everyone is becoming more comfortable with Toast and noticeably quicker on the handhelds. Reminder: complete your loops — once you begin a loop of the room, follow it all the way through before switching tasks. The bartop stayed consistently busy; Sophia kept service tickets moving while Alex engaged guests at point.

**Kitchen:** Lighter night. Chef James did his thing and had guests asking for him!

**Went well:** Creative seating, using the Garden. **Do better:** Working to completion, finishing loops, owning your section.

**Maintenance:** Kitchen low-boy left cover needs a new hinge; curtains coming off rail.

**Favorite moment:** A four-top so happy sitting in the 20s they didn't want to move to a bigger table when it became available.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative:
**MG — Saturday, July 18, 2026** (AM: Sam & Lex/Shannon; PM: Justin/Braden and Marcus/Shannon/Drew, entered by Alexis)

**Sales split:** MB Morning $1,462 | MB Evening $8,990 | Sun Club $4,369 | Hot Eye $1,844. Event sales $3,467 (engagement party on the mezzanine). Total net $16,666 vs target $14,000 (+19.0%). Guests: 56 AM + 236 PM (OpenTable). Comps $377. (Food sales field reported as $0 — not broken out tonight.)

**Morning MB:** A pretty quiet Saturday breakfast that never truly popped off. Two servers on the floor, about 4 tables between 11 and 2. Bar saw first guests at 1; quarter-fullness held into happy hour.

**Evening MB:** Very busy night with a lot of very happy guests. An engagement party took over the mezzanine, finished around 8:30/9. MB was in full swing up until close with a lot of larger parties doing full experiences. We tried reinstating assigned sections instead of rotational seating and it went very well — a learning process for reassigning tables after cuts. Late close; kept some hands to polish a massive amount of silverware. Whole team effort.

**Sun Club:** Steady day on the roof, some hotel guests lingering past close.

**Hot Eye:** Very quiet start, shifted around 10pm with larger parties and hotel guests in for multiple rounds. Lots of new faces and tourists. Finished strong with the service industry crowd till close. Shoutout to James for cleaning up the bathrooms while we closed down.

**Kitchen:** Kitchen did great the past two days, especially tonight — busy but a very smooth, organized shift, no lows or 86s.

**Events:** Smooth engagement party taking over the mezz; everyone out by 9:30.

**Maintenance (URGENT):** The pump stopped working and sewage backed up into Hot Eye. The bathrooms in the lobby and Hot Eye are unusable. James mitigated the damage!

**Favorite moment:** Guests visiting all the way from Toronto hanging out and having a grand ole time in THE.
